headline: Buying at 30% discount to NTA of $4.71, yielding 7.4%, with bond yield peak as catalyst for capital return on top of income
reasoning: Both speakers hold CLW in their portfolios. The REIT has sold off significantly since late 2025, trading at a roughly 30% discount to its net tangible asset value of $4.71. The portfolio yields 7.4% at current prices. The hosts argue that long WALE commercial properties with inflation-linked rents (often to government tenants like Dan Murphy's) have an embedded replacement cost floor. They believe bond yields are near their peak and that when yields decline, CLW will deliver capital appreciation on top of the income yield. They draw a close empirical link between the CLW share price and Australian bond yields.
quote: We hold this REIT, which is the Charter Hall Long Way REIT, ASX, CLW. It has taken a bit of a shellacking. Probably sort of sold at late 2025. But the thing about this is that the further it falls, the more the yield. I think that's pretty good. And in a yield-starved world, it's yielding 7% according to the overlord that is Google finance... the net value of the Charter Hall Long Way REIT... the value of those assets, net of debt is $4.71. So you're buying it at what, 30% discount at the moment... If we're right on bond yields peaking, then you're going to get the capital return and the income from this point onwards.
